reconcile.note: Matthew Henry argues Paul delegated baptism to co-workers so he could focus on preaching, not that he slighted Jesus's baptismal commission.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg sets the Great Commission's baptismal mandate directly against Paul's own disclaimer that Christ did not send him to baptize.

quotes.text: “Go ye, therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them” (Matthew xxviii, 19). Was the penitent thief baptized? Paul says: “I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius.... For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel” (1 Corinthians i, 14, 17).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), sec. on baptism, on Matthew 28:19 and 1 Corinthians 1:17.

sides.snippet: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the Gospel--not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ wouldn't be made void.
